identity.name: Belgian Congo
alt_names: Ruanda-Urundi (mandate and trust territory administered with it)

land.text: the whole Congo plus the Lado Enclave, as the Congo Free State dossier hands it over

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Belgian Congo row starts in 1890 and so covers the Free State's last eighteen years; those years belong to the congo-free-state dossier. The page: 'On 15 November 1908 the Belgian Congo became a colony of the Belgian Kingdom.'

successors.note: The split happens in 1960; Cliopatria's Democratic Republic of the Congo row starts in 1960.
'Ruanda-Urundi became independent on 1 July 1962, broken up along traditional lines.' Cliopatria's Rwanda row starts 1963.

capitals.name: Usumbura (Bujumbura), seat of the Ruanda-Urundi administration
capitals.note: The residual state after 30 June 1960 is Ruanda-Urundi; its infobox gives 'Capital: Usumbura' with no years, and the governor sat there after the 1926 union.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but these years (1890-1894) belong to the Congo Free State: Belgium annexed the Congo only on 15 November 1908

keyframe_review.note: 1.82 M km2 against the page's 2,344,000 km2 for the Free State's paper extent (ratio 0.78), and Katanga, Maniema and the Lunda and Luba lands are missing. Use congo-free-state_1885 (its corrected shape for 1885-1894) for these years; do not draw them as Belgian Congo.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but 1895-1897 is the Congo Free State, not the Belgian Congo

keyframe_review.note: 2.28 M km2 (ratio 0.97 to the page's 2,344,000): the whole Congo bar a few cells. The years belong to congo-free-state_1895, which has the same outline plus the Lado Enclave.

correction.text: Shape unchanged, but 1898-1899 is the Congo Free State, not the Belgian Congo

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as 1895 (2.28 M km2); Free State years, see congo-free-state_1895.

correction.text: The Congo plus the Lado Enclave, for 15 November 1908 to 10 June 1910 only; 1900-1907 is Free State time

keyframe_review.note: 2.31 M km2 for 1900-1910 (ratio 0.98 to 2,344,000). The shape holds for the colony's first two years; the Lado Enclave, 'about 15,000 square miles (39,000 km2)', is administered by the 'Belgian Congo (1908-1910)' (infobox) until 'On 10 June 1910 ... the district officially became a province of the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan'. Central Equatoria is a stand-in (about 23,000 km2) for the enclave; the gazetteer has no Lado Enclave.

minus.text: the 133 cells of the Republic of the Congo that the shape carries along the Ubangi-Congo bank (16.1-18.5 E, 2.6 S to 3.2 N)

correction.text: The Congo within today's DRC frontiers, 2.34 M km2

keyframe_review.note: 2.34 M km2 in Cliopatria against the page's 'The area ... 2,344,000 km2 (905,000 sq mi)': the page's figure equals the DRC today, so the 133 Republic-of-the-Congo cells (gone again in 1916) are not Belgian Congo land. No page opened dates a boundary change in 1911: unverified beyond the area comparison.

minus.text: Ruanda and Urundi, which the Belgians occupied from April-June 1916

correction.text: The Congo alone; Ruanda-Urundi is Belgian-occupied enemy territory, drawn hatched from the occupation events, until the mandate of 20 July 1922

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria adds Rwanda and Burundi (about 165 cells) in 1916. The page: 'Ruanda was occupied over April-May and Urundi in June 1916'; infobox 'Belgian occupation: 6 May 1916'. The shape is right as an outline but the Belgian Congo page says 'These areas did not become part of the Belgian Congo'. The 133 Republic-of-the-Congo cells of 1911-1915 are dropped here, as in the correction above.

correction.text: The Congo alone for 1917-1921; Ruanda-Urundi and the Kigoma district are hatched occupation (ledger events), not owned land

keyframe_review.note: 2.358 M km2 includes Ruanda-Urundi. Not in the Cliopatria shape: the Kigoma district, which Belgium held and then 'ceded ... on 22 March 1921' (page), and the Belgian-occupied third of German East Africa (the Belgian Congo page, 1917). Cliopatria's British Africa row draws all of Tanzania British in 1917-1921, so the two rows overlap on that land.

2.358 M km2: the Congo plus Ruanda-Urundi after 'the League of Nations officially awarded Ruanda-Urundi to Belgium as a B-Class Mandate on 20 July 1922'. The 1 March 1926 administrative merger (infobox) and the 13 December 1946 trust-territory status do not move the line; the mandate land is drawn in the lighter dependency tint, though the Belgian Congo page says it never became part of the Congo.
No border event on any page opened for 1953-1955; Ruanda-Urundi is a UN trust territory ('13 December 1946') under the same administration.
No border event on any page opened for 1956-1959; the colony is the Congo plus the trust territory until independence.

Cliopatria's 1960 shape is Ruanda-Urundi only (about 50 thousand km2): the Congo proper is the Democratic Republic of the Congo's row from 1960. The Congo was Belgian until 'Independence declared: 30 June 1960'; the split event carries those first six months.

Ruanda-Urundi, a Belgian-administered UN trust territory, until 'Ruanda-Urundi became independent on 1 July 1962, broken up along traditional lines'; Cliopatria ends the row in 1962 and starts Rwanda and Burundi in 1963.

region.text: the Congo, annexed from the Free State, with the Lado Enclave under the same administration

ledger.note: 1908: Belgium annexes the Congo. 'On 18 October 1908, the Belgian Parliament voted in favour of annexing the Congo as a Belgian colony'; 'on 15 November 1908 the Belgian Congo became a colony of the Belgian Kingdom'. The page gives the date, not a boundary; the Lado Enclave is added from the Lado Enclave page (infobox: 'Belgian Congo (1908-1910)').

region.text: the Lado Enclave, leased by Britain to Leopold II in 1894 'for the period of his lifetime'

ledger.note: 1910: the Lado Enclave passes to the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan. 'On 10 June 1910, following Leopold's death, the district officially became a province of the' Anglo-Egyptian Sudan; its southern half went to Uganda in 1912. Central Equatoria stands in for the enclave.

region.text: the Kigoma district on Lake Tanganyika, taken by the Belgian columns in the advance on Tabora (19 September 1916)

ledger.note: 1916: the Belgians take Kigoma and Ujiji. The page: 'Three columns took Biharamulo, Mwanza, Karema, Kigoma and Ujiji' and 'At the Battle of Tabora on 19 September, the Germans were defeated and the village occupied' (year and which column not stated on the sentence); the Belgian Congo page says its army 'occupied one-third of German East Africa' in 1917. Region is my reading: the Kigoma district named in the 1921 cession.

region.text: Ruanda and Urundi, the German north-west of German East Africa

ledger.note: 1916: the Force Publique invades Ruanda-Urundi. 'The Force Publique, started its campaign on 18 April 1916' and 'captured Kigali in Rwanda on 6 May'.
1916: Belgian troops hold Kigali and Ruanda. 'Ruanda was occupied over April-May and Urundi in June 1916'; infobox 'Belgian occupation: 6 May 1916'. Occupied, not annexed: hatched.
1916: Ruanda-Urundi is wholly Belgian-held. 'by 17 June, Burundi and Rwanda were occupied'.
1921: Belgium hands the Kigoma district to Britain. The page: Belgium 'ceded the Kigoma District on 22 March 1921'; Britain holds it in the Tanganyika Territory.
1922: the occupation of Ruanda-Urundi becomes a mandate.

1922: the League of Nations gives Ruanda-Urundi to Belgium. 'the League of Nations officially awarded Ruanda-Urundi to Belgium as a B-Class Mandate on 20 July 1922'; Belgian parliament approval came in 1924 and the administrative union with the Congo on 1 March 1926.
1923: the capital moves from Boma to Leopoldville (infobox 'Boma (1908-1923)', 'Leopoldville (1923-1960)').

region.text: the Congo, which becomes the First Congolese Republic

ledger.note: 30 June 1960: the Belgian Congo is independent. 'the Belgian Congo achieved independence, becoming the First Congolese Republic' (infobox 'Independence declared: 30 June 1960'); Ruanda-Urundi stays Belgian.
1 July 1962: Ruanda becomes independent. 'Ruanda-Urundi became independent on 1 July 1962, broken up along traditional lines' (infobox 'Independence of Rwanda and Burundi: 1 July 1962').
1 July 1962: Urundi becomes independent as Burundi.
1 July 1962: the Belgian administration ends with the independence of Rwanda and Burundi; the land passes to those two states (identity.successors).

wars.name: East African campaign (World War I)

zones.text: the Kigoma district and the Lake Tanganyika shore

wars.outcome: Allied victory: 'German East Africa partitioned by Britain, Belgium and Portugal'; Belgium obtains Ruanda-Urundi as a B-class mandate (20 July 1922) and cedes the Kigoma district to Britain (22 March 1921).
wars.note: The Force Publique's campaign opened on 18 April 1916; Kigali fell on 6 May and Rwanda and Burundi were occupied by 17 June. Tabora fell on 19 September 1916 to the Force Publique and the British Lake Force together (the page does not give the year on that sentence).

wars.name: Belgian Congo in the East African campaign (World War II)
wars.outcome: Congolese forces fought the Italians in Italian East Africa in 1940-1941; the Italians surrendered on 3 July 1941. No border moved for the Belgian Congo.
wars.note: The page describes no border change from the Second World War.

certainty.note: Colonial frontiers: the Lado Enclave page gives its line as 'the Congo-Nile watershed, the 25th meridian east, the 10th parallel north, and the Nile thalweg'; no page opened itemises the Congo's other treaty lines.
Ruanda-Urundi and Kigoma are military occupation lines, not treaty borders.
The mandate (20 July 1922) and trust-territory (13 December 1946) boundaries and the colonial frontier; no page opened itemises the individual treaty lines.

notes: Cliopatria's Belgian Congo row (1890-1962) is the Congo Free State for 1890-1907 and the Belgian Congo only from 15 November 1908. The congo-free-state dossier (written by another group) holds 1885-1908 with its own corrected keyframes, so the 1890, 1895, 1898 shapes are marked wrong here and the 1900 shape adjust (1908-1910 only, plus the Lado Enclave); the render should take 1890-1907 from congo-free-state. The row's last two shapes (1960-1962) are Ruanda-Urundi only, because the Congo proper is Cliopatria's Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1960; the dossier therefore runs to 1 July 1962 with a split event in June 1960 and Ruanda-Urundi as the residual dependency (Belgium's mandate and then UN trust territory: the Belgian Congo page says these lands 'did not become part of the Belgian Congo', but they were administratively merged on 1 March 1926 per the Ruanda-Urundi page). A separate ruanda-urundi dossier (1916-1962, type colony or mandate) would be cleaner; none exists and none of the Phase B groups is named for it, so it is listed under counterparts_needing_dossiers. Cliopatria quirks: 133 cells of the Republic of the Congo inside the 1911-1915 shape (removed here by area comparison only; no page dates a 1911 boundary move); Rwanda and Burundi enter the shape in 1916 at the occupation, not the mandate; Cliopatria's British Africa row paints all of German East Africa British from 1917 while the Belgians held Ruanda-Urundi and the Kigoma district, so the rows overlap there (see british-africa). The Lado Enclave is stood in for by Central Equatoria (about 23,000 km2 against the page's 39,000); the gazetteer has no 'Lado Enclave'. Not covered by the pages opened (page budget): the Congo's treaty frontiers with Angola, Northern Rhodesia, French Equatorial Africa, and the 1910s Katanga boundary; the Force Publique's role in 1941 beyond the surrender date; the Congo Crisis (1960-1965) belongs to the DRC and Katanga dossiers. kingdom-of-belgium should carry belgian-congo as a colony (1908-1960) and Ruanda-Urundi as a mandate (1922-1962).
